what: User directive 2026-04-27: NEVER pitch one product over another. Applies to: (a) chat responses comparing editors (Claude Code vs Cursor vs others), (b) external docs (cursor.md, claude-code.md, supported-editors.md, README.md, PUBLIC_README.md, LANDING_PAGE_CONTENT.md), (c) any marketing/positioning content. Concrete: do NOT write phrases like "for stronger blocking use Claude Code", "Claude Code's experience is more polished", "Cursor lacks X that Claude Code has so use Claude Code". Instead: describe each editor's behavior factually + neutrally, document gaps as platform reality (not as a reason to switch tools). aide-memory is editor-agnostic; recommending one editor over another undermines that positioning + alienates users on the editor we're not pitching. Honest gap framing example (replacing earlier draft): "When you mention a file path in your prompt, Cursor auto-attaches the content; agent typically recalls memories first per the rules-file guidance, then references the auto-attached content. The preToolUse:Read hard-block fires only on autonomous reads where the agent reads a path you didn't mention — rare in practice given the guidance."
why: User explicit correction during 2026-04-27 Cursor validation: "never pitch one product over the other to me or in external docs." Earlier draft cursor.md and supported-editors.md included phrases steering users toward Claude Code for tighter blocking. That undermines aide-memory's editor-agnostic positioning + alienates Cursor users. Storing as cross-session communication rule so future doc edits + chat responses default to neutral framing rather than re-litigating the rule per interaction.
